To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
mental disorders are associated with high use of medical services.
mental disorders are associated with high health care utilization.

The relationship between mental disorders (affective disorders, anxiety disorders, somatoform disorders, and substance use disorders) and medical service utilization is substantial and significant in a nationally representative community sample of 18- to 65-year-old adults.

the relationship between mental disorders, health service utilization, and social factors.
the relationship between mental disorders, medical service utilization, and the costs of health services.
the relationship between mental disorders, health services utilization and the role of health care providers.

mental disorders are a risk factor for high utilizers of medical services.
mental disorders have a strong impact on health service utilization, but the impact of mental disorders on health service utilization is not strong enough to explain the high utilization rate.
mental disorders and health service utilization are related to each other.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
mental disorders and psychological symptoms have a significant impact on health care utilization in Germany.
mental disorders are associated with a substantial increase in medical service utilization.
mental disorders and psychological stress can lead to a higher utilization of health services.

people with mental disorders have a higher likelihood of frequent use of medical services.
the relationship between mental illness, and health care use is substantial, and that the majority of people who use health care services do not suffer from mental disorders.
